title: FEC Administrative Improvements Act
official_title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require electronic report filing for persons making certain electioneering communications and to permit political committees to make disbursements other than by check.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Joseph Morelle (D-NY) with 3 cosponsors. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action; no Senate action is recorded.
summary: Makes two changes to the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971. Section 2 amends 52 U.S.C. 30104(a)(11)(A)(i) so that the electronic filing requirement covers persons who "make[] electioneering communications," not just those making expenditures. Section 3 rewrites 52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1) to let political committees make disbursements by means other than a check drawn on the committee's account.
brief: Requires electronic FEC filing for persons making electioneering communications and lets political committees pay by methods other than check.

top_lines.headline: Disbursements No Longer Check-Only
subs: Strikes "except by check drawn on such accounts in accordance with this section"
Inserts "except from such accounts" in its place

items.main: Names the Act the "FEC Administrative Improvements Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Amends section 304(a)(11)(A)(i) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30104(a)(11)(A)(i)) by inserting "or makes electioneering communications" after "expenditures."
items.detail: The bill does not otherwise change the electronic-filing regime in section 304; it only expands the class of filers covered by that clause.

sections.label: Section 3 — Permitting Political Committees to Make Disbursements by Methods Other Than Check

items.main: Amends section 302(h)(1) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1)) by striking "except by check drawn on such accounts in accordance with this section" and inserting "except from such accounts."
items.detail: The bill's new language keeps the account-based limitation but removes the requirement that disbursements be made specifically by check.

gaps: The bill does not specify which non-check payment methods are permitted or set FEC rulemaking on the point.
The bill does not restate the definition of "electioneering communications," which is set in the underlying Federal Election Campaign Act and is not reproduced here.
The bill sets no effective date, so the timing of implementation depends on the general rule for enactment.
The bill does not describe how the FEC's existing electronic-filing infrastructure will be adapted to the newly covered filers.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Steil
featured_quotes.text: There is a lot of work to be done to update our campaign finance laws for the digital age, and this is an important piece of legislation. I encourage all my colleagues to vote in favor of H.R. 8738.

added: "or makes electioneering communications" added to 52 U.S.C. 30104(a)(11)(A)(i)
modified: 52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1) reworded from "except by check drawn on such accounts in accordance with this section" to "except from such accounts"
